diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Kayhan newspaper wrote that the enemy must hear the roar of Iran's new missiles at American bases in various countries including Germany and Britain. The newspaper added that a network of missile cities and deep tunnels of the IRGC has spread across Iran. Kayhan also wrote that these strategic bases deep underground guarantee the country's great deterrent capacity.

Prince Reza Pahlavi described the Islamic Republic as a jihadist, militant, and transnational movement that has turned Iran into a global terrorism base during the ceremony receiving the King Solomon Award in Krakow, Poland. He said the people of Iran are the first hostages of the Islamic Republic and are fighting the same forces that threaten Jews and the free world. The King Solomon Award was presented to him by the European Jewish Association.

The Public Relations of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army announced that at dawn on Wednesday, 20 Aban, a tanker caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz due to hitting a naval mine. The Islamic Republic Army described this tanker as "violating". The Navy also stated that it controls the eastern Strait of Hormuz and safe passage of ships requires coordination with the armed forces of the Islamic Republic.

Prince Reza Pahlavi, during a visit to the Auschwitz camp in Poland, emphasized the necessity of education about the Holocaust and confronting its denial. He also called for global support for the Iranian people's struggle against the Islamic Republic.

Alireza Mansourian, former coach of Al-Talaba Iraq, signed a six-month contract to lead Al-Zawraa. Al-Zawraa is currently sixth in the Iraqi Stars League with 21 points, and Mansourian will face his former team Al-Talaba in his first match. He said his contract is initially for six months and may be extended if conditions are favorable.

Bahman Nouri, governor of North Khorasan, announced that despite the implementation of water supply projects, 90 villages in this province still face water stress. Resolving this issue depends on continuing infrastructure projects and securing financial resources. The ongoing water shortage in these villages has made access to sustainable drinking water difficult for residents.

Sohrab Kihani, a member of the Medical Sports Federation Treatment Council, reported the first surgery on the leg of Paria Mehrmand, an injured basketball player of the Sahar Academy team, in Tehran and stated that the next 24 to 48 hours are critical for determining the treatment process of this athlete. Mehrmand, who was severely injured on 17 Aban in a bus rollover accident of the Sahar Academy team, was transferred to Tehran on Tuesday, 19 Aban, after vascular graft surgery in Khuzestan and is currently hospitalized in a private hospital. Kihani said doctors in Khuzestan successfully restored blood flow in the injured leg through vascular grafting, and the medical team in Tehran has improved oxygen delivery to the leg somewhat through surgery and washing of the injured area.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic, threatened the US and Israel with harsher attacks in a message on the fifteenth anniversary of Hassan Tehrani-Moqaddam's death. He warned that any point that becomes a threat center against the Islamic Republic will be a direct target of asymmetric operations by the armed forces. Abdollahi emphasized that this threat is within the existing capabilities of the Islamic Republic's armed forces.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international affairs analyst, said about 20 terrorist plots and extraterritorial actions related to the Islamic Republic have been identified in the US and Europe. He added that cyber activities have become one of the Islamic Republic's operational tools for retaliation. Alizadeh referred to a reported cyberattack on cooling systems of hundreds of stores in France and an attack on the Ferford military base in the UK, saying these actions could increase concerns of European countries and the US about threats attributed to the IRGC.

The COP 31 meeting in Antalya continues with discussions on topics including food and agriculture, energy, and transportation, and a leaders' summit is also being held at this conference. Farzia Sabti, a reporter from Iran International, reports from the venue of this meeting.

Tehran's prosecutor announced charges against a woman following the release of a video on social media. A judicial case has been opened for this citizen, and two of her social media accounts have been blocked by judicial order.

The Boston Celtics won against Philadelphia 123-101 in a game where Paul George shined. The match ended with Boston rising to the top of the Eastern Conference standings with 9 wins and 2 losses. Paul George was the star of the game, scoring 36 points and making six successful three-pointers.

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, said at the Knesset inauguration ceremony that the only way to permanently eliminate the threat of the Islamic Republic is to overthrow the rule of the Ayatollahs. He added that despite heavy blows, the Islamic Republic still seeks the destruction of Israel and the revival of its nuclear program.
A video sent to Iran International shows that a group of Iranians supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi in Hamburg, Germany, chanted "Fatemeh Sepahri must be freed" in support of this political prisoner.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, arrived in Antalya to participate in the 31st CAP summit. According to the announced program, bilateral meetings with officials from various countries, including the President of Turkey, are scheduled for Pezeshkian on the sidelines of this summit.
The head of the Tehran Province Judiciary announced the issuance of flogging sentences and other punishments for defendants in three cases related to currency violations.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, stated that the Islamic Republic will not remove any portion of its enriched nuclear materials from Iran. He said the Islamic Republic needs enriched materials for designing nuclear ships and submarines and has reached an advanced level in electronic warfare that allows controlling and downing American drones. Rezaee warned that any new US attack targeting Iranian military bases will be responded to, and ending the war on all fronts in West Asia, especially Lebanon, is one of the Islamic Republic's essential conditions.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on a street wall in Bandar Abbas and said, "Long live Iran until the overthrow of the Islamic Republic."

Morteza Kazemian, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the positions of the Islamic Republic officials show that the survival of the regime is a priority over national interests and people's livelihoods. He added that in the past eight years, the dollar rate has risen from about four thousand tomans to 270 thousand tomans, and people's purchasing power has sharply decreased.

The social emergency expert of Khorasan Razavi Welfare Organization reported increased concerns about child abuse and suicide attempts in this province and said child abuse is the most frequent issue reported to the social emergency hotline 123. In the first six months of the year, out of about 8,000 social emergency missions, 20% were related to child abuse and 16% to suicide attempts.
Early today, three citizens were killed following indiscriminate shooting by military forces at a passenger car and its occupants in the Lakshak area of Zahedan.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said there is a possibility of intensified maritime and economic blockade of the Islamic Republic by the US. He added that continuing this situation could severely reduce the government's financial ability to cover military and suppression forces' costs. Ghazizadeh also said that if pressures continue, the Islamic Republic might be forced to reach an agreement with the US, start a military conflict, or attack ships and oil infrastructure of regional countries.

One day after France identified the IRGC as responsible for a cyberattack on its stores, concerns about cyber threats in Italy increased. The Italian National Committee for Public Order and Security, chaired by the Interior Minister, is reviewing recent cyberattacks, potential hacker targets, and vulnerabilities of public institutions' information and communication systems.

It was reported that Michael Carrick, Manchester United's coach, despite speculation about his dismissal, appeared on Wednesday morning at the Carrington training complex and showed a thumbs-up sign to photographers. According to Daily Mail, club officials are expected to decide to end cooperation with Carrick due to the team's poor results, and Mauricio Pochettino has been introduced as the main candidate to replace him. Also, Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner of Manchester United, is scheduled to discuss the future of the team's bench, and if Carrick is dismissed, compensation payments to the coaching and management staff will reach about 30 million pounds.

Shargh newspaper reported that although about 85 percent of the country's schools are public, between 85 to 90 percent of the seats in top universities are allocated to graduates of non-public schools. Official bodies have stated that public schools have recorded the lowest average grades for the second consecutive year, indicating an educational gap between public and non-public schools.

The Kermanshah Intelligence Department reported the arrest of five individuals in the provinces of Kermanshah, Alborz, and Tehran. Connection with Israeli and American intelligence services was cited as among the reasons for their arrest.

A video published on social media shows a conversation between two citizens about the quality of flour. One of them says the material in the flour is not bran but poultry feed. A baker also says he has not seen such flour in over two decades of working in this profession.
On Tuesday, 19 Aban, smoke rose from Didamar Island in Oman in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media attributed this incident to an attack by the IRGC Navy on navigation aid systems.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the Chinese side must believe that the Islamic Republic will not trade its relations with China for its relations with the West. He added that strengthening relations with Beijing is very important and should be viewed with a long-term perspective. Boroujerdi also referred to the serious and special emphasis of the late leader on relations with China.

According to reports, Farang Lak, the mother of Hamid Basiri, died on Tuesday, 18 Aban. Family close ones said she developed cancer two months after her son's killing and died before the first anniversary of his death. Hamid Basiri, 35, was targeted during the protests on 19 Dey in Fardis, Karaj.

Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, said about the possibility of his presence in the National Olympic Committee presidential election that many friends insist strongly but he has no motivation and has not yet decided. He added that personally he has no desire to participate but friends insist that he should help. Dabir also said that he has never even prepared a resume for himself in his entire life.

The Tabnak website strongly criticized Mehdi Taj and Amir Ghalenoei, describing the decision to send Iran's national football players to Iraq by land as disregard for Iran's dignity and respect. The media wrote that after the cancellation of the direct flight permit for the national team to Basra, football officials should have reconsidered their decision. Tabnak also described this action as treason to the homeland and failure to preserve the country's dignity.

The case of Peyman Farahavar, a political prisoner sentenced to death, has been referred to the enforcement branch. His death sentence was previously confirmed by Branch 39 of the Supreme Court. He informed his family by phone on Tuesday, 18 Aban, about the referral of his case.

NATO has started a five-day exercise for submarine detection and tracking in the Baltic Sea with the participation of eight countries and the presence of thousands of military personnel, warships, and patrol aircraft. This exercise is being held while NATO considers Russia its main military threat.

Ata Hosseinian, an economic and energy journalist, said the Islamic Republic is preparing public opinion for gasoline priced between 50,000 to 70,000 tomans by gradually limiting free gasoline distribution and increasing gas station prices. According to him, the government, considering the naval blockade and inability to import gasoline, intends to align domestic consumption with refinery production and gradually increase prices.

Alisina Mostafavi, a mountaineer, musician, and nature and animal lover, was executed in Kerman Central Prison. He was executed on Wednesday, 22 Mehr, after a closed trial, amid reports of torture and forced confession. This report was published by Farbod Sarvandi from Iran International.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations regarding the non-use of children in military affairs, more than 320 students from Dorud in Lorestan province and Varamin and Pardis in Tehran province were sent to operational areas in the south of the country as part of camps called "Rahian-e Noor".

The Director General of Crisis Management of Isfahan Province announced that in the first half of the current year, 474 workers in the industrial sector of Isfahan Province, including mining, construction, and industrial fields, have been involved in accidents.

The case of three suspects linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps accused of planning an attack against Iran International journalists has entered the final decision-making stage by the jury in the UK. On the third day of deliberations, the jury members must reach a unanimous verdict. Mostafa Sepahvand, Shapur Ghal'eh Alikhani Nouri, and Farhad Javadi Manesh are accused of spying for the Islamic Republic's security agencies against two Iran International journalists.

Reza Talaeinik, spokesperson for the Ministry of Defense of the Islamic Republic, wrote on the social network X on Wednesday, 20 Aban, that Iran's military backing relies on strategic productions and advanced technologies. He added that Iran's defense capability has been strengthened and the fate of the war is clear: either acceptance of Iran's rightful demands or the enemy's surrender on the battlefield.

Several Shahin car voucher holders protested in front of Saipa's customer service department on Wednesday, 20 Aban, against the non-delivery of their cars. According to them, after three years since registration and payment, they have neither received their cars nor had their money refunded.

A court session was held to address the charges against 5 journalists named Mandana Sadeghi, Arash Ghaleh Golab, Kourosh Karam Pour, Farzaneh Yahyaabadi, and Reza Mohammadi at Branch 103 of the Criminal Court Two in Abadan County.

Foreign ministers of the G7 countries in the final statement of the Paris meeting declared that the Islamic Republic "must never" acquire nuclear weapons and if there is no diplomatic solution, they will continue economic and political pressures. They also emphasized full implementation of reinstated sanctions and accused the Islamic Republic of supporting non-state armed groups and providing military aid to Russia. The G7 members condemned Iran's attacks on neighboring countries and disruption of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and called for an end to these attacks.

The UN Climate Conference, COP 31, is being held in Antalya, Turkey, with a dual leadership structure and climate negotiations led by Turkey and Australia. The preliminary programs focus on Pacific island countries, and the event is hosted in a coastal tourist city. Addis Ababa has been announced as the host of the UN Climate Conference in 2027.
Citizens reported to Iran International that stores refuse to accept ration cards, charge higher prices for goods, and limit the items that can be purchased.

Giuseppe Valditara, Italy's Minister of Education, said evacuated schools received the same message and the number of schools receiving it is expected to increase. He considered the widespread sending of this message as a sign of the threat's lack of credibility. Giorgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, emphasized that these threats do not pose a danger and the police are monitoring the situation.
The US Secretary of State emphasized Lebanon's independence and said that decisions about the country's future should be made by the Lebanese government and army, not the Islamic Republic.

A report has been published about the increase in advertisements for selling body organs in some streets of Tehran. ILNA stated that some citizens, especially workers and low-income groups, due to financial debts and livelihood pressures, have resorted to selling kidneys, liver, bone marrow, and other body organs.

According to information received by Iran International, the intelligence forces of the Abu al-Fadl base in Ahvaz arrested two brothers named Omid Ahmadi-Nejad and Chamran Ahmadi-Nejad on the evening of 28 Mehr 1405. Chamran Ahmadi-Nejad was released on bail one week after his arrest, but there is no information about the status or whereabouts of Omid Ahmadi-Nejad. Omid Ahmadi-Nejad's family has had no contact with him since his arrest, and the detaining security agency has refused to provide information about his health despite the family's persistent inquiries.

The insurance company Allianz has estimated that physical damages from a war with Iran in the Gulf countries have exceeded 200 billion dollars. More than 80 energy facilities have been targeted, with major damages to energy infrastructure in Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain. Allianz predicts that the economic losses of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries will reach 790 billion dollars by 2030.

Paria Mehrmand, a 15-year-old basketball player and member of Iran's national youth team, who was severely injured in the bus rollover accident of the Sahar Academy team, still faces the risk of permanent damage to her right leg. Her father expressed concern about her condition and has asked the Minister of Sports to form a team of specialist doctors for urgent care of Paria's situation. Paria's right leg has developed a severe infection and much of its muscles have been lost due to impaired blood circulation.

A video shows that during the commemoration of Matin Abbasi's birthday at his grave, his mother said her son is now "a son of Iran." Matin Abbasi, 19 years old, was shot dead by officers on 19 Dey 1404 in Tajik Boulevard, Sabashahr.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the statement by the G7 foreign ministers about the Islamic Republic, despite emphasizing continued political and economic pressures, is not commensurate with the level of threats posed by the Islamic Republic against Europe. He added that the Islamic Republic has carried out some of its threats on European soil and countering it requires practical and comprehensive actions beyond statements and verbal threats.

Mohammad Baharmast Ziyabari, a resident of Ziyabar in Somesara county, has been in detention since 16 Aban. He was transferred to the West Gilan penitentiary after being arrested by intelligence agents of the Revolutionary Guards. He faces charges of propaganda against the regime.

Abu Mujahid Al-Assaf, the security official of Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq, stated that the group will not retreat in support of the Islamic Republic and will not allow its enemies to target it alone. He said Kata'ib Hezbollah will remain alongside its allies in Yemen and Lebanon until the last breath and will not give up its weapons under any pressure. Al-Assaf also accused the Iraqi Prime Minister of participating in the siege of the Islamic Republic under US orders and criticized the Iraqi government's cooperation with Washington.

Mes Shahr-e Babak club announced that Mojtaba Hosseini, after an agreement with the club's managers, replaced Ghasem Shahba and took charge of the Mes Shahr-e Babak football team. Hosseini, who started the current season with Nassaji Mazandaran, was previously considered one of Yahya Golmohammadi's assistant candidates for Iran's U23 team, but ultimately accepted Mes Shahr-e Babak's offer. Mes Shahr-e Babak, with only five points from 12 matches, is in eighteenth place in the standings and is considered one of the main candidates for relegation.

Bahareh Shahmehri, a 17-year-old protester from Nishapur, was killed by a gunshot on 19 Dey. According to information received by Iran International, security agencies pressured her family to accept the government's narrative and introduce their child as a martyr.

A group of Havaniruz employees protested today in front of the Kermanshah governor's office over the uncertainty of their housing cooperative project. The protesters stated that they bought land in 1390 but after 15 years the housing construction project has not yet been implemented.

Joe Biden, former US president, was targeted with thrown milk packets by Palestinian supporters in Dublin and took shelter behind an umbrella for protection. At the same time, police clashed with protesters and Biden was escorted by officers to his SUV.

A group of Iranians living in Hanover, Germany, held a protest on the evening of 19 Aban against the executions in Iran. Participants in the gathering expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi and emphasized the need to raise awareness in German society about repression in Iran.

The head of the judiciary in Langarud announced the issuance of an alternative sentence to imprisonment for an environmental offender by the third branch of the peace court in this county. The accused was sentenced to pay a fine and plant 40 saplings of forest tree species at the crime scene.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said Mojtaba Khamenei has issued an order allowing the armed forces to operate without geographical limitations if necessary. Naqdi added that the armed forces can respond appropriately anywhere in the world if the enemy makes the slightest mistake.

Zhila Sadeghi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, was released from Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan on Tuesday, 19 Aban, after posting a bail of three billion tomans. Sarir Moghann, her daughter, was also released on 28 Mehr with the same bail amount. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Dani Danon, Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, said during a visit to the Auschwitz-Birkenau camp that the Islamic Republic still seeks the destruction of Israel. He emphasized that the international community cannot repeat the slogan "Never Again" while legitimizing "inciters of hatred and killers" at the UN. The visit was held within the framework of the working group against anti-Semitism, with dozens of ambassadors including Germany's ambassador attending.

One day after the IRGC unveiled its new missile city, Israel unveiled the advanced Super Ice cruise missile that can penetrate the IRGC's underground concrete shelters. At the same time, Netanyahu emphasized that the only way to eliminate this existential threat against Israel is to overthrow the Ayatollah regime.

Senior world officials gathered in Antalya to discuss the transition to clean energy, investment in green industries, waste management, and methane emission reduction on the first day of the climate summit. The main focus of the talks is finding solutions to reduce pollution and greenhouse gas emissions without jeopardizing energy security and economic growth. Farzia Sabti, a reporter for Iran International, reports.
Videos sent show that a protesting citizen wrote the slogan "Long live the Shah" and the phrase "18 and 19" in memory of the martyrs on the walls of Tehran's streets.

An arrest warrant for Ali Kalateh Dolati, a detainee related to the January 1404 protests, was issued by Branch 7 of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Sabzevar. The charges include brandishing a weapon, illegal buying, selling and possession of weapons and ammunition, assaulting officers, propaganda against the regime, connections with exiled elements and hostile states, and attempted murder.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, threatened in an interview with Al Mayadeen network that if the US attacks Kuh-e Kolang, the IRGC will respond with broader attacks and will further reduce its offensive limitations.
A video received by Iran International on Wednesday, 20 Aban, shows the poor quality of tap water in Ahvaz.

Canada's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has reimposed economic sanctions on the Islamic Republic, placing 11 key entities of the regime back on the blacklist that had been removed in 2016 after the JCPOA agreement. These entities include Iran's energy, financial, and nuclear sectors; among them are the National Oil Company, National Tanker Company, National Bank, Mellat Bank, Industry and Mine Bank, and Iran Insurance.

The second day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the US in Abu Dhabi ended with announced progress on some issues, including security matters and prisoner exchanges. US representatives stated they will travel to Moscow to meet Vladimir Putin to discuss the results of the Abu Dhabi talks and ways to advance a peace agreement.

Mohammad Mashinchian said in the program "Chortkeh" that many workers have been forced to have multiple jobs to cover living expenses, and some effectively leave the labor market because their work costs exceed their income.

Amirhossein Sadeghi, former captain of Esteghlal, said that Alireza Ildarom, the assistant referee of the Esteghlal and Esteghlal Khuzestan match, caused "Yaser Asani's reputation to be damaged." He also considered the suspension of Ildarom and the apology of the referees committee officials to Esteghlal fans as useless.
The Iranian women's national futsal team won the bronze medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, achieving Iran's first-ever team medal in Olympic and Youth Olympic competitions.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Baharestan county announced that in the past three months, 35 commercial units in this county have been sealed for various reasons, including what has been called "moral crimes."

Four independent labor and retirees organizations issued a joint statement criticizing Mohammad Reza Aref's remarks about the link between wage increases and inflation. They protested the decline in workers' purchasing power and the gap between wages and living costs. The signatories emphasized the need to improve economic and living conditions for workers and collective action to pursue their demands.

According to reports received by Iran International, a government cleric interrogated young students ideologically in a school about their participation in last December's protests. The cleric claimed to have attended the protests and to be a supporter of Reza Shah Pahlavi. This action was a cover for security projects to identify protesters in educational environments and caused fear and concern among students and their families.

David Barnea, former Mossad chief, called for a full blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and continued economic sanctions instead of renewed war with the Islamic Republic at the Israel Hayom conference in New York. He considered the likelihood of an agreement that the Islamic Republic would adhere to as low and said Tehran seeks nuclear weapons in the long term. Barnea also supported Donald Trump's policies and said Hamas and Hezbollah have been weakened.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in an interview with Al Jazeera that the Islamic Republic does not differentiate between the US and Israel in negotiations or war, and if either starts a war, it will respond to both. He added that the US must implement seven conditions of the Islamic Republic to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations, and the Strait will not return to its pre-war status. Ghalibaf also announced reaching an understanding with Oman regarding shipping routes and a vessel traffic separation system in the Strait of Hormuz.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the moment of an explosion at the Ferochrome Baft factory in Kerman province, which he said occurred on 12 Aban and left 10 injured. The citizen reported repeated explosions, prevention of informing the labor office, severe pollution, and the layoff of nearly 100 employees. The number of factory workers is now about 80.

Hossein Sobhani, head of the Islamic Council of Rey County, announced that about 22 buses operate in Qiamdasht, a significant portion of which are worn out and some are over 20 years old. He said frequent breakdowns and poor service quality do not meet the needs of citizens and about 13,000 students of the Islamic Azad University East Tehran branch. He also said the owners of these buses lack sufficient financial capacity to renew the fleet and necessary support and facilities have not been provided.

It was reported that the costs of medical services and basic goods in Iran have sharply increased. A person said that a surgeon took a 50 million toman bribe for his son's surgery. Also, the prices of ECG, espresso coffee, jacket zipper repair, simple burger, and eyeglass frames have significantly risen.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, threatened that if the US attacks again, American military bases in distant regions and even Europe will be targeted. He emphasized that Tehran will not allow even a tiny amount of enriched uranium to leave Iran and has informed Russia of this stance. Meanwhile, Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the Commander-in-Chief of the IRGC, said Mojtaba Khamenei has authorized operations anywhere in the world.
A citizen from Bojnord sent a video to Iran International saying that the subsidized flour given to people is full of lice and asked how people are supposed to use this flour.
Niusha Saremi reported that Mojtaba Khamenei has authorized cross-border operations of the IRGC. It was also said that the US and Israel are preparing for confrontation.

Some workers of Homan Gohar Ayandeh Company in the industrial town of Konarak complain about repeated delays in salary payments, working about 14 hours daily, unpaid overtime, and delays in insurance payments, and have called for responsible authorities to intervene. Former workers of Parsilon textile factory in Khorramabad, unemployed and uncertain for about 10 years, have reported the plan for the fourth public auction of the unit and expressed concerns about the capability of the new buyer.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that while the US government talks about continuing economic pressure and naval blockade instead of war and some media report progress in negotiations, field evidence indicates readiness for the possibility of military conflict.

A video released on social media shows the restlessness and grief of the mother of the missing Peyman Pourdavarani in the absence of her son. Peyman, 31 years old and father of one child, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Kerman.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi announced on the evening of Wednesday, 20 Aban that Ali Zaghi and Ilya Akbari, two young men arrested during the national uprising of Dey month, face imminent execution. The Mashhad Revolutionary Court, headed by Hossein Yazdankhah, has sentenced these two young men to death. Additionally, four other young men in the Shandiz case have also been sentenced to death.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced on Wednesday, 20 Aban, that Washington seeks a "complete victory" in the war and does not intend to accept any result less than that. He said rebuilding what the US has destroyed will take 25 years and hopes not to have to destroy more parts of the country. Trump also said Iran has been at war against the US since 1979 and that the US did not start the war.

On Wednesday, 20 Aban, a group of Havaniruz employees protested the uncertainty of the housing cooperative project by staging a sit-in in front of Kermanshah Governor's Office. Also, employees of the Isfahan Regional Electricity Company held a protest in front of their company building. Yesterday, Shahin voucher holders gathered at the Saipa administrative building to protest the non-delivery of their registered vehicles despite payment and missed deadlines.
It was reported that the Iranian government has issued a military ultimatum to NATO and European countries.

The Law on Regulation and Supervision of Border Trade and Sustainable Employment for Border Residents, approved on 25 Bahman 1402, obliges the government to plan for sustainable employment, sufficient income, and proper social security. The main question is how these obligations will translate into clear and actionable support in daily life. This issue is especially relevant for porters whose income depends on border trade.

A video released on social media shows the restlessness of the mother of the disappeared Ghazal Janqorban at her grave. Ghazal, 15 years old, was shot by suppressors during the public protests on 19 Dey in Isfahan and died in the hospital.

More than 135 days have passed since the arrest of Fatemeh Jami, a citizen of Gorgan, and she is still being held in Gorgan prison without a clear status. A source close to her family has confirmed this. The court hearing for her case is scheduled for 1 Azar.

Kiumars Heydari, deputy chief of staff of the Islamic Republic Armed Forces, said the confrontation with the US has turned into a regional war and the enemy's interests and military bases are within range of the Islamic Republic's missiles and drones. He added that the armed forces' response will be without geographic limitation and if an aircraft takes off from a country to attack Iran, the armed forces are allowed to target a similar target in that country. He also said the armed forces' target bank for a possible future war has been updated and covers points in the region and beyond.
In the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad, a warning of an attack on Europe by the Islamic Republic was raised.

Alireza Koushki, Esteghlal player, said he went three times close to death due to a severe injury. He explained that an elbow hit from a young player caused a rib fracture and pressure on his lung. Doctors stated about 50% of his lung was filled with air, and he has undergone a difficult treatment period.

Adidas celebrated the farewell to the German national team by printing images of German football legends on the last jersey designed for the team. The German Football Federation's contract with Adidas ends at the end of 2026 after 72 years, and Nike will design and produce the German national teams' kits thereafter. The upcoming FIFA international match dates will feature Germany's last games wearing Adidas kits.

Israeli company Rafael unveiled the "Super Ice" cruise missile with a 454-kilogram warhead. Farzin Nadimi said this missile, with a speed close to the speed of sound and advanced guidance systems, can target from farther distances with greater accuracy. Nadimi added that the more powerful warhead and increased resistance to navigation disruptions have enhanced the missile's operational capability, and it is still unclear to what extent these technologies will be used in a potential conflict with the Islamic Republic.

A new wave of bomb threats against schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, and Italy has led to the emergency evacuation of several educational centers. Italian officials stated that about 6,300 schools have been affected by these threats. Reza Talebi said Russia might be using cyber groups and networks linked to the Islamic Republic to create crisis and increase divisions in European societies.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, said they will not allow even a tiny amount of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran. He added that these materials will remain for domestic use in Iran and that the Islamic Republic is designing nuclear-powered ships and submarines. Rezaei also said that in the future, these materials might be used to build small modular reactors.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that a power struggle over Ali Khamenei's legacy has escalated. He added that after Khamenei's death, power factions within the IRGC have clashed to seize a larger share of power and wealth and to eliminate their rivals. He also said that the battle between Mohsen Rezaei and Baqer Qalibaf has become one of the most visible manifestations of the power struggle at the top of the Islamic Republic.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that after Khamenei's death, the power struggle in the Islamic Republic intensified. He added that Qalibaf, who had long aspired to the presidency, tried to present himself as beyond the president and as the main decision-maker of the system. Qalibaf claimed to have coordinated the heads of the branches of power, IRGC commanders, and managed the war.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said if no agreement is reached between the US and the Islamic Republic, a military attack by the US and Israel will inevitably happen sooner or later; because Washington and Tel Aviv consider the Islamic Republic's potential acquisition of nuclear bombs and intercontinental missiles a threat to their national security.

Despite expectations for a reduction in tensions in the war between the Islamic Republic and the United States, attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz continue. According to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, at least 10 ships were targeted in the first 10 days of November. The Islamic Republic has claimed responsibility for attacking three oil tankers on Sunday, 17 Aban [Gregorian: 2026-11-08].

The New York Times on Wednesday, 20 Aban, reported citing three Iraqi officials and one American official that Washington's weeks-long effort to persuade Iraq, Turkey, and Pakistan to close border crossings with Iran has so far been unsuccessful. The US has requested the closure of all Iranian border crossings except two, but Baghdad has rejected this request. After diplomatic efforts failed, the US Central Command formed a 20-member task force called "Iron Gate" to counter the transfer of weapons and sanctioned goods through Iran's borders.

Iran International's investigation shows that Parsian Bank has been managed for years by the Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order. The Order appoints the bank's managers and has gradually transferred the bank's shares to its subsidiary holding, Tadbir. Key figures from the Order are present at the bank's top levels.

Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Instagram the start of production of his first TV series called "Day 1s." The series is about a British agent in the football transfer world and is being made in collaboration with Matthew Vaughn. Ronaldo will be the executive producer of the series and may also appear on camera.

Shahram Khaledi said Russia's new proposal on the Islamic Republic's nuclear program should be viewed within the framework of Moscow's competition with Washington. He added that Moscow does not want Iran to gain the capability to build nuclear weapons and may be seeking a way out of the crisis. Khaledi also mentioned the possibility of Iraq mediating between Tehran and Washington, saying Baghdad may be trying to create conditions for an agreement.

Baharan Azadi, author of two articles about the widespread gas outage, was a guest on the program "With Kambiz Hosseini" to discuss people's accounts of the outage and its impact on their daily lives in Iran.

Kambiz Hosseini warned of an unprecedented gas outage and a harsh winter in Iran. Some children go to school with blankets, and the government’s plan to keep people warm is saving energy. The term "energy imbalance" reflects the reality of people's lives with cold homes and worried elderly and students.

Saudi Civil Defense announced that remnants of two ballistic missiles fired by Yemeni Houthis towards the Mecca region fell on Wednesday in areas including the village of Sabouha after being intercepted and destroyed. On the same day, the Saudi-led military coalition reported intercepting and destroying a drone in the eastern region of the country. The eastern region of Saudi Arabia, which hosts major oil and gas reserves and key Aramco facilities, had also been targeted by drone attacks in recent days.

A video published on social media shows the poor condition of Taq Kasra, a structure over 1400 years old near Baghdad. The video shows the area around this historical heritage site filled with garbage, depicting neglect of one of the architectural masterpieces of the Sasanian era in the heart of Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire.

G7 foreign ministers condemned the destabilizing policies of the Islamic Republic in the final statement of the Paris meeting and called for full implementation of the reinstated UN sanctions. They deemed maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the security conspiracies of the Revolutionary Guard in Western countries unacceptable. G7 member countries warned that if a diplomatic solution is not reached, economic and political pressures on the Islamic Republic will intensify.

Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, spokesperson for the Pakistan Army, stated that his country is ready to take all necessary measures to defend Saudi Arabia based on the joint defense agreement and the Makkah Pact. He emphasized that Pakistan's commitment to Saudi Arabia's security is non-negotiable and confirmed that Pakistani forces are currently present in Saudi Arabia with defensive, support, and exercise missions. The meeting on 26 October of representatives of the Makkah Pact member countries with officials of the Islamic Republic in Tehran was held to reduce tensions and strengthen regional cooperation.

The Wall Street Journal reported, citing American and regional officials, that JD Vance, the Vice President of the United States, is considering direct negotiations with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic. Vance is leading Washington's diplomatic efforts to reach an agreement with Tehran, and Donald Trump has approved his role in these negotiations.

Simultaneously with concerns about the execution sentence of Peyman Farahavar, a prisoner poet in Lakan prison in Rasht, the office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the risk of executing death sentences for six detainees of the December national uprising. According to the statement, Ali Zaghi, Ilya Akbari, and four other young men have been sentenced to death in the so-called Shandiz case. The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi called for widespread information dissemination to prevent the execution of these sentences.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations lecturer, said that Donald Trump seeks to use the full military and economic capacity of the US to gain more concessions from the Islamic Republic. He added that Trump does not desire a large-scale war and tries to reach an agreement by oscillating between negotiation and economic pressure, which he can present as an achievement to the American public.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board of directors has considered removing Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, after the disclosure of his second extramarital affair. One of these relationships was with a woman suspected of collaborating with China's intelligence agency. Nvidia's board was scheduled to decide on Huang's future on Wednesday.
